tlsFixInput.scope: Narrow review of TLS scheme enforcement, related changed assertions and summary derivation

findings.title: TLS row could accept a plaintext READY address
findings.originalRisk: package_probe compared the requested TLS profile against a run.py summary derived from the certificate argument. Service did not reject http:// when a certificate was supplied, so HTTP/1 TLS could pass over plaintext.
findings.resolution: Service checks the actual READY scheme before requests, certificate and hostname validation stay enabled, and summary TLS derives from the observed https scheme.
findings.closure: Independently read the changed assertions; source fix closes the stated false-pass path. Parent readback records all 12 original TLS rows as https.

findings.title: Next-statement window started after INSERT completion
findings.originalRisk: An intervening Execute pipelined while INSERT was blocked could precede CommandComplete and be omitted from the next-business-statement check.
findings.resolution: The command window now starts after the INSERT command_sequence (dispatch), with only at most one exact pinned SQLx catalog query permitted before the separate operations SELECT.
findings.closure: Independently read the one-condition fix. Parent readback records both original actual PG JIT/AOT traces satisfying the stricter window, with no intervening command before INSERT completion.

checks: Conflict uses a real held upstream COMMIT, independently observed pg_locks/pg_blocking_pids wait, zero-row INSERT completion, separate winning-row SELECT and durable HTTP/result/effect equality.

Unknown suppresses actual PostgreSQL COMMIT and idle ReadyForQuery replies before closing the connection; HTTP must report outcome_unknown with identity-bound recovery, then durable recovery and same-key replay remain equal.

The SQLx metadata exception is a full-match catalog-only shape with bounded numeric OID/attribute pairs, no generic SELECT wildcard, at most one intervening metadata command and a recorded statement hash; verified against pinned sqlx-postgres 0.9.0 ColumnResolver source.

Package/source/controller snapshots, isolated NuGet cache, exact package versions/archive hashes, artifact inventories, native-output hashes and refusal of changed resume inputs establish the intended reproducible artifact chain.

Actual process execution supplies the RuntimeFeature JIT/AOT marker. Edited source changes are compiled, and distinct DTO content plus handler header are observed over HTTP while native bytes remain fixed.
TLS clients retain certificate and hostname verification; HTTP2 frame probes also require ALPN h2. The strict READY scheme check closes the HTTP1 TLS inference gap.

PATH traps detect ordinary cargo/rustc/rustup invocation and are checked after commands and rows. Their claim remains an isolated consumer check, not absence of every absolute-path Rust executable or a pristine-machine proof; the controller explicitly leaves B24 pristine and B22 soak acceptance false.
